newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rice eases as buyers sidelined, Japan eyed.
newsitem.headline: Thai rice eases as buyers sidelined, Japan eyed.

text.p: Thai rice prices dropped this week in the absence of fresh demand as buyers were sidelined awaiting the price to fall further on the back of rising supplies, trade sources said on Thursday.
The market eyed a 20,000-tonne rice tender to be held in Japan next week, hoping that Thailand would be able to secure a share, traders said.
Rainfall had improved in most of the rice producing areas after a long dry spell and farmers had started planting, dispelling fears that the 1997/98 first crop would be severely affected, they said.
More supplies of this year's second crop rice were available in the market and prices were expected to dip lower.
"There are buyers waiting in the wings. They just waited to see where the bottom is before stepping in," said a trader at a major trading house.
"Exporters also stayed out as they had bought enough to cover short-term demand. Therefore, the FOB market was quite quiet this week," he said.

But in a local retail market, rice trade was active as consumers scrambled to hoard rice due to misunderstandings that rice was subject to a new 10-percent value-added tax which was due to effect on Saturday.
The commerce ministry issued a statement to calm local buyers, saying the VAT did not apply to rice.
At a Bangkok port, nine vessels were loading 52,755 tonnes of rice for shipment to Iraq, Malaysia, Japan, and Indonesia.
Thailand has so far shipped 2.88 million tonnes of rice this year compared to 3.43 million during the same period last year.
